historical_reviews.v3_1: Active-session inventory is security-sensitive even when read-only; member identifiers must be treated as scoped evidence rather than ordinary logs.

original_test_intent: Read the intended BMC's active Sessions collection, validate collection identity, reported count and unique member links, and preserve a time-bounded redacted inventory without creating, deleting or opening individual sessions.
original_method: Retain one GET to the source-exact Sessions collection, replace embedded credentials/TLS bypass with trusted secret-safe access, and validate collection invariants without following member links.
manual_activity: The security/BMC owner approves active-session inventory access, supplies trusted least-privilege credentials, and defines whether member IDs may be retained or must be pseudonymized/redacted.
required_inputs: BMC endpoint bound to immutable SUT identity
safety_requirements: Do not expose credentials, tokens or Authorization
Do not retain raw session IDs outside approved evidence
No session create/delete or log clearing
agent_execution_scope: Issue one bounded Sessions collection GET
Capture status/headers/raw JSON securely with timestamp
Reconcile Members@odata.count with unique in-namespace links
Audit no member access or mutation
engineer_actions: Approve active-session inventory and identifier handling
Provide schema/profile and any expected-session comparison source

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The endpoint matches and `.Members[].Id` can enumerate identifiers, but `-k`, basic-auth argv and full listing are unsafe; the filter also omits HTTP/schema/count, duplicate-link and namespace checks.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: With trusted TLS and secret-safe least-privilege authentication, GET /redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions once, capture a timestamped snapshot, validate SessionCollection identity/count/unique member links without following them, and export only approved pseudonymized metadata.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The exact collection path, GET intent and 15/10 timing remain; no expected session count or member IDs are inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat the response as an atomic active-session inventory: verify collection schema and count/link consistency at one timestamp, then pseudonymize identifiers and avoid member expansion.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds trusted transport, collection integrity, snapshot timing and privacy controls instead of a full readable listing.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: SessionService validates service capability and a Session member validates one authorized context; this case alone proves only collection topology at the captured instant.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Sessions can appear or expire during observation, so comparisons must use one captured response rather than multiple live reads; identifiers reveal active management topology and require restricted handling.

project_override_considerations: A Redfish SDK is equivalent only if it makes one non-expanding collection request, preserves certificate binding, exposes raw count/link data for validation and applies the approved identifier transformation.
expected_evidence: Credential-provider and schema/parser versions without secrets
Request/snapshot timestamp and HTTP status/content type
Members@odata.count reconciled to unique in-namespace links
No member GET, session mutation or log clearing

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item, source path, GET command and DeepSeek endpoint consistently identify the Sessions collection. Weak privacy and validation criteria are deficiencies, not contradictions.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The collection purpose and operation are explicit. Trust, credential, schema and privacy/redaction inputs are concrete prerequisites.

review_improvement: Turns a raw session-ID dump into a timestamped, count-consistent and privacy-controlled collection inventory without member expansion.
independent_technical_reasoning: A live Sessions collection is volatile; issuing separate reads for count and IDs could manufacture inconsistencies as sessions expire. One response must therefore be captured and its reported count reconciled with unique member links from that same snapshot. Link paths must remain under the intended collection, and identifiers should be pseudonymized before portable evidence is produced. Following a member would change both privacy exposure and testcase scope.
